title: God Exists
content:
When I was nine years old, I was hit by a car while riding my bike. I was thrown 75 feet and landed on my head, injury which crushed part of my skull (it was about a pear-sized hole over my right parietal lobe). A surgeon and his wife were packing their car for a weekend trip and witnessed the accident. The surgeon immediately responded and gave me CPR and mouth- to-mouth while his wife called 911. In the three minutes it took for the ambulance to arrive, I lost a third of my blood on the pavement. I was rushed to the hospital where I was given a blood transfusion. My ruptured spleen was removed and over the course of the next eight hours shards of bone were removed meticulously from my brain by two neurosurgeons. My vital signs dropped and I fell into a coma.

My prognosis for survival was very poor. According to my mom, at one point during surgery the doctor informed my parents that my vital signs had dropped dangerously low and they feared losing me. He asked my parents if they had any religious affiliation for which he could call clergy. My mom said she looked at me through the window of the operating room and said, “Isn’t he beautiful.” She told me that it was following this moment that my vital signs began to climb steadily, which could not be explained medically.

Meanwhile, I vividly recall the experience of seeing myself from above the operating table and looking down. There was a bright light near me, which I believe may have been the operating room light. As I looked down I saw only silhouettes, but I knew that was me lying on the table with all kinds of activity and movement going on around me. Then I was removed from the scene and surrounded by darkness, nothingness, but fully enveloped in the peace and love of God’s presence. I recall the feeling of wanting to stay with him. But, then I had no ability to think, or make any decisions whatsoever. The last thing I remember, which I believe to be the most memorable of this whole experience, is the conviction I had from God, "Regardless of what happens, it’s going to be okay." The next thing I remember is waking from my coma four days later in the intensive care room and seeing sunlight from the window illuminate the lime green wall of my room. According to my mom, I answered the doctor correctly when he asked how many fingers he was holding up. My recovery was slow. A double polymer plate was wired into my skull with titanium. I had physical therapy for about six months until I regained my fine motor coordination skills on the left side of my body. Some smells and flavors seemed different (particularly chicken and green beans), but these returned in about a year or so. Nevertheless, I have since made a full recovery from this accident with no residual effects, despite all prognoses, odds, and phenomena unexplained by medical science. I have no spleen, take no medication, and am healthy. The most significant thing I take from this experience is the conviction that God exists, loves me and has a purpose and plan for my life. Neither of my parents were believers nor did I have any spiritual upbringing. Regardless, I knew without a doubt at the time that I was in God’s presence surrounded by his incomprehensible peace and love, and I wanted to be with him but it wasn’t my time. This experience planted a seed in my life, a foundation of spirituality and faith, which did not come to fruition until many years later.

demographics.religious_background_detail: Neither parents were believers; no spiritual upbringing (later faith developed years later).

diagnosis.diagnosis_raw: Traumatic brain injury with crushed skull (pear-sized hole over right parietal lobe), massive blood loss, ruptured spleen; coma.
diagnosis.disease_name: Severe traumatic brain injury (skull fracture with bone fragments in brain) with hemorrhagic shock and ruptured spleen; coma
diagnosis.severity_description: Life-threatening trauma; very poor prognosis; coma; major neurosurgery
diagnosis.prognosis_given: Prognosis for survival was very poor; doctors feared losing him during surgery.
diagnosis.quality_of_life_impact: Coma; later impaired fine motor coordination on left side requiring physical therapy.
diagnosis.primary_site: Right parietal skull/brain (described as pear-sized hole over right parietal lobe)
neurological_deficits: impaired fine motor coordination on left side (temporary)

treatment.treatments_raw: CPR and mouth-to-mouth; ambulance transport; blood transfusion; splenectomy; neurosurgery removing bone shards from brain over 8 hours; ICU coma care; skull repair with double polymer plate wired with titanium; physical therapy ~6 months.
treatment.surgery_type: Splenectomy; neurosurgery removing bone fragments; later skull reconstruction with polymer plate/titanium wiring
treatment.surgery_outcome: Survived; later full recovery; no residual effects reported; no spleen.

remission_outcome.time_to_remission_raw: Woke from coma after four days; slow recovery; physical therapy for about six months; sensory changes resolved in about a year; later full recovery.
remission_outcome.verification_detail: Woke from coma after 4 days; answered physician’s finger-count question correctly; later reports full recovery with no residual effects.

turner_factors.spiritual_practices_raw: Direct experience interpreted as God’s presence; later foundation of spirituality and faith (came to fruition years later).
purpose_sources: belief that God loves him and has a purpose/plan for his life
turner_factors.purpose_details: Conviction after the experience that God exists and has a purpose and plan for his life.

pre_illness_state.pre_illness_description: No spiritual upbringing; parents were not believers.

existential_shift.identity_shift_description: Conviction of God’s existence and love; foundation of spirituality and faith planted by the experience.
existential_shift.transformation_narrative: Most significant takeaway was conviction that God exists, loves him, and has a purpose/plan; experience planted a seed of faith that matured years later.
existential_shift.pivot_point_description: During NDE/OBE: enveloped in peace/love; received conviction/message: 'Regardless of what happens, it’s going to be okay.'
existential_shift.transformation_timing: Experience occurred during surgery/coma; faith matured years later.

anomalous_experience.experience_description: Vivid out-of-body perception above operating table; then darkness/nothingness with profound peace and love interpreted as God’s presence; received conviction/message that everything would be okay.
anomalous_experience.experience_timing: During surgery/coma after accident (before waking 4 days later).
anomalous_experience.message_content: "Regardless of what happens, it’s going to be okay."

correspondential_markers.correspondence_notes: Narrative emphasizes spiritual awakening/faith foundation after NDE rather than pre-illness psychological causation.

validation.statistical_improbability_notes: Severe pediatric head trauma with massive blood loss, splenectomy, prolonged neurosurgery and coma; family reports unexplained improvement in vital signs after mother’s moment of awe; narrator reports full recovery despite poor prognosis.
validation.extraction_notes: Not a cancer/remission case; outcome is recovery from severe traumatic injury. Remission fields mapped to recovery outcome; limited objective follow-up documentation (no imaging/labs/dates).

analysis.case_summary: At age nine, the narrator suffered life-threatening polytrauma (severe skull/brain injury, massive blood loss, ruptured spleen) and entered a coma after extensive neurosurgery. During surgery/coma he reports an NDE with an out-of-body perspective and a message from God; he later awoke after four days and ultimately made a full recovery despite a poor prognosis.
key_healing_factors: Emergency medical intervention (CPR, transfusion, splenectomy, neurosurgery, ICU care, skull reconstruction, physical therapy)
Reported NDE/OBE with profound peace and a reassuring message
Later-developed spiritual faith and sense of purpose
unique_features: Surgeon witnessed accident and initiated CPR immediately
Mother reports unexplained improvement in vital signs after an emotionally significant moment
Classic NDE elements: OBE, light/darkness, peace/love presence, message
analysis.analysis_notes: Narrative describes recovery from traumatic injury rather than spontaneous remission of disease. Timing and durability of ‘no residual effects’ are not dated; verification is primarily narrative with some clinical details but no records, imaging, or named clinicians.
